Thanks again for the demo earlier — appreciate the run-through. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can prioritize: 

- Main use case: clinician-facing summarization of encounter notes, streaming results into UI so clinicians can act before the full doc completes.
- Concerns we saw in the prototype: partial outputs sometimes repeat or cut mid-sentence; stop sequences aren't always respected (we got a few truncated tokens and odd trailing punctuation); and occasional latency spikes that make the UI jitter.
- We want to validate model fit for clinical summarization (fidelity + safety) and have a small eval to compare recommended models.

Could you: 
1) Share the recommended model variants for this workload and a short plan for the eval (prompt sets, metrics, expected deliverables)?
2) Provide a streaming-specific checklist or tuning knobs we can try to improve partial output coherence and stop sequence behavior?
3) Let us know what data/sample prompts you need (I attached a quick sample_prompts.txt) and an estimate for turnaround.

Thanks — Ellen

Hi Ellen — great to hear the demo was useful and thanks for the clear notes (and the prompt set you attached). Quick recap and proposed next steps below.

Recap from Redwood: 
- Primary goal: low-latency, high-fidelity clinician summaries streamed into the UI while minimizing hallucination and ensuring stop sequences end generated text cleanly.
- Recommended models for initial evaluation: redwood-13b-chat (base), redwood-rlhf-13b (safety-tuned), and a quantized candidate redwood-13b-8q for cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Streaming candidate for low-latency: redwood-13b-stream (with chunked decoding and smaller emission size).

Proposed eval plan (attach: acme_eval_plan_v1.pdf):
1) We run a 48-hour controlled eval comparing the three model variants on your sample prompts + 200 de-identified clinical notes you provide. Metrics: ROUGE/F1 for fidelity, stop-sequence adherence rate, token-level repetition rate, mean and p95 streaming latency, and a subjective clinical-quality score.
2) Streaming-specific tests: we capture partial-output coherence (a small scorer that looks at next-token predictability), stop-sequence failures (cases where model ignores configured terminators), and render-time latency effects.
3) Deliverables: a benchmark report, a set of tuned streaming parameters (chunk_size, max_latency_ms, emission_threshold), and a short remediation checklist.

What we need from you: 
- A 200-note dataset (de-identified) or a smaller representative sample if you want a quicker turnaround.
- Any hard stop sequences you need enforced (e.g., "--END-SUMMARY--").

We can kick off the eval as soon as next Tuesday, 2026-03-23. If that works I can book a 30-minute alignment to lock the dataset and metrics.

Links: evaluation doc (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcEvalDocsAcme) and HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/ACME-2026-Q2-1579).

- Latency: our SRE saw p95 spikes up to ~1.2s on some calls during the demo. Can you share the knobs to prioritize p95 vs cost (we prefer p95 < 600ms if feasible)?

Hi Ellen — quick triage from the infra/serving side (cc Marissa). Thanks for the sample prompts — they were helpful. A few concrete items we can run immediately: 

1) Stop-sequence adherence: we track stop-sequence adherence as part of streaming telemetry. Failure modes we've seen: (a) tokenizer boundary issues where stop tokens split across chunks, (b) overly large emission windows that allow the model to continue past a terminator. Mitigations: reduce emission window (chunk_size) and enforce a post-processing cutoff that drops tokens after a matched stop sequence (we can add a conservative truncation layer for your sensitive fields).

2) Partial-output repetition: often caused by decoding temperature/presence_penalty interplay and by aggressive prefix caching misalignment for very short prompts. For the initial eval we'll try: temperature=0.2, presence_penalty=0.1, and enable small adaptive prefix caching.

3) Latency: p95 spikes typically come from cold KV-cache misses and occasional GC pressure on the serving host. For p95 < 600ms we recommend: redwood-13b-stream on dedicated capacity with prefix caching enabled, batch_timeout_ms=10, and max_concurrent_requests tuned to your quota. Also consider redwood-13b-8q if cost becomes binding; it typically lowers p95 by ~20-30% in our tests at the cost of some fidelity.

We can run the streaming-specific eval and surface a short set of patch notes — attaching our current notes (streaming_latency_patch_notes.md). If you share the 200 notes, we'll spin up the eval and push a telemetry shard to the Drive folder so you can watch p50/p95 live.

Jordan Blake
